author: kkb
text:
Hello! I would like to ask a question about compression:) Maybe not about CP itself but about proper naming.

See attached chart:

We know that the place marked as 1 is CP: price rises and tests DPs at the same time (clears demand).

But I wonder if the place marked as 2 could be also called compression? Or should I call it just consumption?

The idea is similar: price is in demand and with time the pockets of demand residing below are cleared. Each time price visits the demand it makes lower highs. So I conclude that the demand is exhausting. When all the demand is consumed, price can fall easily.

Thanks!

author: DrSwing
text:
kkb wrote: Each time price visits the demand it makes lower highs. So I conclude that the demand is exhausting. When all the demand is consumed, price can fall easily.

Yes I would agree with that kkb, your No. 2 is consumption.

author: kkb
text:
Hi! The large red pole down suggest that there could be compression to the left (the wicks of the candles also gives that clue). But from this timeframe it is hard to be sure (for me:P). I would switch to 1D TF and mark all demand in this area and also mark when the demand is visited.

According to your question "New supply..." - if your compression (left) is really compression then yes, it is a great supply. Because always on the compression boundaries there are many orders. So the place where compression breaks (and FTR is made) is always an important place:) Also look how price left this level - large pole down without stopping - it also suggests that there are still many orders to be filled (which is proved when price returns to this level).

Best, Chris
